description: Insurance is a financial arrangement that protects individuals and businesses against losses arising from uncertain future risks in exchange for a premium.

mcq.questionText: What is the main purpose of insurance?

options.text: To make the insured person rich after a loss
To provide protection against financial loss caused by uncertain risks
To increase the number of traders in a country
To replace the work of commercial banks

mcq.explanation: Insurance compensates the insured for losses from uncertain events; it protects rather than enriches.

mcq.questionText: The regular payment made by the insured to the insurance company is called the:
mcq.explanation: A premium is the consideration the insured pays, usually periodically, for insurance cover.

mcq.questionText: A written contract between the insurer and the insured that sets out the terms of cover is known as the:
mcq.explanation: The insurance policy is the legal document containing the agreed terms and conditions of the contract.

mcq.questionText: Which principle requires both parties to a contract of insurance to disclose all material facts honestly?
mcq.explanation: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) demands full and honest disclosure of all material facts by both parties.

mcq.questionText: The principle that ensures the insured is restored to the same financial position as before the loss, without making a profit, is:
mcq.explanation: Indemnity places the insured back in the financial position held before the loss, preventing profit from insurance.

mcq.questionText: Insurable interest means that the insured must:

options.text: Pay the premium in cash only
Stand to suffer financially if the insured item is lost or damaged
Own more than one insurance policy
Be employed by the insurance company

mcq.explanation: Insurable interest exists when a person benefits from the survival of property and would suffer loss from its damage.

mcq.questionText: Which type of insurance protects cargo, ships and freight against losses at sea?
mcq.explanation: Marine insurance covers risks connected with sea transport such as loss of the ship, cargo and freight.

mcq.questionText: Under the principle of subrogation, after paying full compensation the insurer is entitled to:

options.text: Take over the rights of the insured over the damaged property
Refuse to pay any future claims
Increase the premium for all customers

mcq.explanation: Subrogation transfers the insured's rights in the salvage or against third parties to the insurer after full payment.

mcq.questionText: When property is insured with more than one insurer, the principle that shares the loss among the insurers is:
mcq.explanation: Contribution ensures each insurer pays a fair share of the loss so the insured is not over-compensated.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is generally an INSURABLE risk?

options.text: Loss of profit due to poor business management
A fall in market prices because of competition
Destruction of a warehouse by an accidental fire
Changes in fashion and customer tastes

mcq.explanation: Accidental fire is a pure, measurable and uncertain risk, making it insurable, unlike speculative business risks.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a NON-INSURABLE (speculative) risk?

options.text: Theft of goods from a shop
Possible loss from speculating in shares hoping for a profit
Damage to a motor vehicle in an accident

mcq.explanation: Speculative risks carry a chance of profit or loss and are not insurable; insurance covers only pure risks.

mcq.questionText: Life assurance differs from other classes of insurance mainly because:

options.text: The event insured (death) is certain to happen, only the time is uncertain
No premium is paid by the insured
It does not require insurable interest

mcq.explanation: Death is certain to occur eventually, so it is called assurance, while general insurance covers uncertain events.

mcq.questionText: A trader who imports goods worth a large sum can use insurance mainly to:

options.text: Avoid paying any taxes on the goods
Transfer the risk of loss or damage during transit to the insurer
Increase the selling price of the goods
Reduce the quality of the goods imported

mcq.explanation: Insurance allows traders to transfer transit and other risks, giving confidence to trade in large quantities.

mcq.questionText: The form filled in by a person who wishes to take out an insurance policy, giving details of the risk, is called the:
mcq.explanation: The proposal form is completed by the prospective insured to disclose details on which the insurer assesses the risk.

mcq.questionText: By collecting small premiums from many people to compensate the few who suffer loss, insurance operates on the principle of:
mcq.explanation: Insurance pools many small premiums into a common fund used to compensate the few members who actually suffer losses.

fib.questionText: The regular amount of money paid by the insured to the insurer for cover is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The premium is the price paid for the transfer of risk to the insurer.

fib.questionText: The legal document that contains the terms and conditions of an insurance contract is called the insurance _____.
fib.explanation: The policy is the written evidence of the insurance agreement.

fib.questionText: The principle requiring full and honest disclosure of all material facts is known as utmost _____ faith.
fib.explanation: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) binds both parties to disclose material facts honestly.

fib.questionText: The principle that restores the insured to the same financial position as before the loss is called _____.
fib.explanation: Indemnity prevents the insured from making a profit out of a loss.

fib.questionText: The financial stake a person must have in the insured property is called insurable _____.
fib.explanation: Insurable interest means the insured would suffer financially if the property were lost.

fib.questionText: The type of insurance that covers loss or damage to ships and their cargo at sea is called _____ insurance.
fib.explanation: Marine insurance covers hull, cargo and freight risks of sea transport.

fib.questionText: Because death is certain to happen, cover on human life is more correctly called life _____.
fib.explanation: The term assurance is used because the insured event (death) will certainly occur.

fib.questionText: When an item is insured with several insurers, the sharing of the loss among them follows the principle of _____.
fib.explanation: Contribution ensures each insurer pays a proportionate share of the claim.

fib.questionText: Risks that involve a chance of both profit and loss, such as buying shares to resell, are called _____ risks and cannot be insured.
fib.explanation: Only pure risks (loss or no loss) are insurable; speculative risks are not.

fib.questionText: The form completed by a person applying for insurance, giving details of the risk, is called the _____ form.
fib.explanation: The proposal form provides the insurer with information to assess and price the risk.

tf.questionText: Insurance allows a person to make a large profit from a loss that has occurred.
tf.explanation: The principle of indemnity ensures the insured is only restored to the former position, not enriched.

tf.questionText: A premium is the amount of money paid by the insured to the insurer for cover.
tf.explanation: The premium is the consideration paid for the insurer to accept the risk.

tf.questionText: Utmost good faith requires only the insured, and not the insurer, to disclose material facts.
tf.explanation: Both parties to the contract must disclose all material facts honestly.

tf.questionText: A person can insure the life of a complete stranger in whom he has no interest.
tf.explanation: Insurable interest is required, so one cannot insure a stranger in whom there is no financial interest.

tf.questionText: Marine insurance covers risks connected with the transport of goods by sea.
tf.explanation: Marine insurance covers the ship, cargo and freight against perils of the sea.

tf.questionText: The principle of subrogation allows the insured to claim from both the insurer and a third party for the same loss and keep both payments.
tf.explanation: Subrogation passes the insured's rights against third parties to the insurer after full compensation, preventing double payment.

tf.questionText: Insurance encourages trade by giving traders confidence to invest and operate even where risks exist.
tf.explanation: By transferring risk to insurers, traders can invest and expand with greater confidence.

tf.questionText: The death of an insured person is an example of a speculative risk that cannot be insured.
tf.explanation: Death is a pure risk and is insurable through life assurance; it is not speculative.

tf.questionText: Insurance works by pooling premiums from many people to compensate the few who suffer losses.
tf.explanation: Premiums from many policyholders form a common fund used to pay the few who experience losses.

tf.questionText: Contribution applies only when property is insured with a single insurance company.
tf.explanation: Contribution applies when the same property is insured with more than one insurer.

summary.correctAnswer: A contract in which the insurer agrees to compensate the insured for losses from specified risks in return for a premium.
summary.explanation: It transfers the financial burden of uncertain risks from the insured to the insurer.

summary.correctAnswer: The payment made by the insured to the insurer in exchange for cover.
summary.explanation: It is the price of transferring risk to the insurer.

summary.correctAnswer: The written document stating the terms and conditions of an insurance contract.
summary.explanation: It is the legal evidence of the agreement between insurer and insured.

summary.correctAnswer: Both parties must honestly disclose all material facts about the risk.
summary.explanation: Non-disclosure of material facts can make the contract void.

summary.correctAnswer: The insured is restored to the financial position held before the loss, without profit.
summary.explanation: It prevents people from gaining from insurance.

summary.correctAnswer: The insured must stand to suffer financially from the loss of the insured item.
summary.explanation: Without insurable interest the contract is not valid.

summary.correctAnswer: After full compensation, the insurer takes over the insured's rights in the salvage or against third parties.
summary.explanation: It stops the insured from being paid twice for one loss.

summary.correctAnswer: When several insurers cover the same property, each pays a fair share of the loss.
summary.explanation: It prevents the insured from claiming the full amount from each insurer.

summary.correctAnswer: Pure risks (loss or no loss) are insurable, while speculative risks (chance of profit or loss) are not.
summary.explanation: Examples: fire and theft are insurable; trading for profit is speculative.

summary.correctAnswer: It transfers risk, gives traders confidence, encourages investment and supports credit and large-scale trade.
summary.explanation: Reducing the fear of loss helps trade and the economy grow.

hoq.questionText: A trader insured a building worth 20,000,000 shillings with two companies for 20,000,000 each. After a fire causing total loss, how much in total can the trader recover from both insurers combined?

options.text: 40,000,000 shillings, the sum of both policies
20,000,000 shillings, shared between the two insurers
Nothing, because double insurance is illegal

hoq.explanation: By indemnity and contribution, the trader recovers only the actual loss of 20,000,000, shared proportionately between the insurers.

hoq.questionText: A businessman did not disclose that his warehouse was previously damaged by floods when taking fire cover. When a later fire occurred, the insurer refused to pay. Which principle best justifies the refusal?

options.text: Subrogation, because the insurer takes over rights
Contribution, because more than one insurer was involved
Utmost good faith, because a material fact was concealed
Indemnity, because the loss exceeded the policy value

hoq.explanation: Concealing a material fact breaches utmost good faith and can make the contract voidable, allowing the insurer to refuse the claim.

hoq.questionText: Why is it generally NOT possible to insure against losses caused by a fall in the market price of goods a trader is holding for resale?

options.text: Because such a loss is a speculative risk with a chance of profit or loss
Because the trader has no insurable interest in the goods
Because the premium would be too small to matter
Because indemnity does not apply to traded goods

hoq.explanation: Price changes are speculative risks involving the possibility of gain or loss, so they fall outside insurable pure risks.
